auth.mfaDescription: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
auth.forgotDescription: Enter your username. If an account exists, we will send instructions.
auth.forgotSubmitted: If an account exists, instructions have been sent.
auth.lockedDescription: Too many failed attempts. Try again later or contact an administrator.
auth.changeDescription: This account requires a new password before you continue.

errors.generic: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errors.forbidden: You do not have permission to do this.
errors.tooManyRequests: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.invalidCredentials: The username or password is incorrect. Repeated failures delay further attempts.

users.title: Users
users.searchPlaceholder: Search by name, username or email
users.unlockDescription: The account was locked by repeated failed sign-ins. Unlocking lets them try again immediately.
users.disableDescription: They will not be able to sign in until the account is enabled again.
users.enableDescription: They will be able to sign in again.
users.createDescription: The account is created with a one-time password the person must change at first sign-in.
users.initialPasswordHint: A one-time handover credential. Choose something the person can type.

audit.title: Audit
audit.description: Who did what, to what, when, and from where.
audit.dateRangeRequired: Choose a date range to search.
audit.dateRangeTooWide: The range is too wide. Narrow it to 90 days or fewer.

employees.title: Employees
employees.description: People, their unit and their position.
employees.createDescription: An employee is an organizational record: their number, their name, and the unit they belong to. Salary, leave and contract are not here — those belong to the HR application.
employees.employeeNumberHint: A stable, unique number that other systems use to refer to this employee.
employees.noUnitsTitle: No employee can be created yet
employees.noUnitsDescription: Every employee belongs to an organizational unit, and there are none. Build the structure first.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: What a role grants, and where.
roles.name: Name
roles.assignDescription: The role decides what this user can do. The scope decides who to.
roles.revokeDescription: The user loses every permission this role carries, immediately.
roles.scopeUnitAndBelow: A unit and everything beneath it
roles.noAssignmentsDescription: This user holds no role, and so can reach no administrative screen.
roles.cannotEscalate: You cannot grant a permission you do not hold yourself.

organization.title: Organizational structure
organization.description: The company's units, each beneath the one it reports to.
organization.createDescription: The new unit is created beneath the selected unit, or at the top if none is selected.
organization.codeHint: A stable code that does not change, such as FIN or HR-01.
organization.moveDescription: The unit and everything beneath it move together. A unit cannot be moved inside itself.
organization.deactivateDescription: The unit will no longer appear in lists. A unit with active children or active employees cannot be deactivated.
organization.emptyDescription: Start with the company's top unit, then add what sits beneath it. An employee cannot be created before there is a unit for them.

security.title: Security
security.description: Two-factor authentication, and the actions that require your identity confirmed.
security.mfaWhy: Some actions — granting roles above all — ask you to confirm your identity again before they run. That confirmation is not possible without two-factor authentication.
security.enrolStep1: Open your authenticator app and add a new account using this key:
security.enrolStep2: Then enter the six-digit code the app shows:
security.disableDescription: Enter a current code from your app. Without it, anyone holding a stolen session could remove the protection that would have stopped them.
security.recoveryDescription: Save these somewhere safe now. They will not be shown again — they are stored hashed, and this is the only moment they are readable. Each one works once.
security.stepUpDescription: This action needs your identity confirmed recently. Enter the code from your authenticator app.
security.stepUpNotEnrolled: This action needs two-factor authentication, which is off for your account. Turn it on from the Security page, then try again.

dashboard.unavailableHint: You do not hold the permission to read this figure.
dashboard.stepOrganization: Build the organizational structure — no employee can exist before a unit does.
dashboard.stepSecurity: Turn on two-factor authentication — without it you cannot grant roles.
dashboard.stepUsers: Create user accounts and grant them roles.
